# Gevurah Release Critique

> The Awtsmoos renews restraint together with abundance, drawing the line where truth can live; Awtsmoos.com rejects ornamental labor when evidence says the wiser act is to verify, integrate, and give.

## Critique of the maximal wave

- Do not add new semantic authorities merely to increase feature count. The lifecycle/full split already solves the proven composition problem.
- Do not change cache implementation unless the new behavioral tests reveal a real identity or failure-policy defect.
- Do not add browser timing SLAs. Record local measurements, but keep structural graph/resource contracts as the stable guarantee.
- Do not invent typed dependency scheduling from string dependency ids; current ids can represent services.
- Do not add CSP or deployment headers until production header ownership is traced; a local meta policy can break legitimate module imports.
- Do not alter unrelated 19 baseline failures to manufacture a green full-suite number.
- Do not stage from the dirty primary checkout. Fresh-origin integration worktree is mandatory.
- Do not replay any old uncertain mutation; inspect current files and git diff instead.
- Do not push until every mission file has been explicitly classified and the staged diff is inspected.
- Do not deploy a SHA that differs from remote main or from the clean release worktree HEAD.

## Highest-value order

1. Finish focused test verification on the final split files.
2. Fix only evidence-backed regressions.
3. Run existing universal + structural + package/import graph gates.
4. Run full package suite and classify differences against historical baseline.
5. Run fresh v3 browser E2E at 320/390 with navigation, race, busy/live, same-origin, and diagnostic assertions.
6. Refresh docs/evidence with final measurements.
7. Generate planned-vs-actual delta and exact mission file manifest.
8. Integrate in fresh-origin clean worktree.
9. Test staged/integrated state again.
10. Commit, push exact SHA, verify origin.
11. Prepare/activate through audited two-phase release.
12. Public E2E and exact-SHA verification.
13. Only then close REMAINING_WORK.

## Risks demanding special proof

- Upstream main moved while this mission was in progress.
- The primary checkout has unrelated concurrent dirty work.
- Browser resource counts can change as the v3 demo adds small modules; module count changes are evidence, not necessarily regressions.
- Rapid async interaction can expose stale-render races even when normal clicks pass.
- Test-generation files themselves previously crossed the 120-line ceiling, proving structural gates must include tests.
- Public deployment can succeed mechanically while serving stale cache/state; fresh browser and cache-busted requests remain mandatory.
